text:
maya: Heads up — deploybot just quarantined the EU canary during rc-2025.05.03.
deploybot: [automated] Canary deployment blocked: vuln-scan failure on image redwood/service-worker:2025.05.03-canary
deploybot: Vulnerability: CVE-2025-1234 (transitive) libcache v2.1.0 — CVSS 9.3 — path: service-worker -> redis-client -> libcache
maya: ugh. Is this in the base image or app dependency?
ryan: looks transitive from redis-client. I pulled the SBOM from the artifact registry.
sasha: paste: ```sbom.json snippet
"packages": [
  {"name":"libcache","version":"2.1.0","source":"transitive","purl":"pkg:maven/libcache@2.1.0"}
]```
anita: sec-bot, do we have provenance/signature on that artifact?
sec-bot: SBOM provenance check: FAILURE — cosign signature missing for artifact id sha256:abcdef1234
leo: if signature missing + high CVSS, legal will probably ask to block. @legal any quick take?
legal: need evidence of exploitability in our context. If it's purely transitive and not used at runtime, we can consider a scoped mitigation. But missing signature raises chain-of-trust flags — prefer a rollback unless mitigated within change window.
ryan: mitigation options I see: 1) pin to previous redis-client that doesn't pull libcache 2) vendor a minimal patch (hotpatch) into canary image 3) full rollback of canary to previous stable.
maya: timeline? we have a 2h change window remaining for EU. Hotpatch + rebuild + another scan will take ~60–90m. Full rollback is ~10m but costs customer-facing delay.
leo: what's the exploitability? Any PoC?
sasha: no PoC. But CVSS 9.3 suggests remote code exec in certain usage patterns — our integration uses cache-read/write only. could be exploitable.
anita: ops: can we do a regional carve-out? Keep US canary, yank EU, iterate on EU image?
ryan: Deploybot supports regional rollbacks. Command: ```/deploy rollback --env=eu --service=service-worker --to-tag=2025.04.28-stable```
maya: fine with regional rollback if legal ok. downside: divergent fleets and customer segmentation in telemetry.
legal: regional rollback acceptable as a temporary measure; require postmortem and evidence of final fix before full rollout.
sec-bot: note: SBOM missing signature must be resolved before global rollout per policy ID: SBN-3.
leo: can security accept a timeboxed hotpatch + signature attach? If sec signs off on new artifact and we re-run canary scans, we can attempt EU redeploy in the same window.
anita: I can assemble a minimal patch branch and build a new image. Need CI minutes and someone to watch the rollout.
ryan: I'll schedule the regional rollback now and queue a rebuild. Executing rollback in ~5m unless objections.
maya: +1 do it. Notify EU on-call.
leo: @deploybot please execute rollback and tag the incident.
deploybot: [automated] Starting rollback: /deploy rollback --env=eu --service=service-worker --to-tag=2025.04.28-stable — initiated by ryan
deploybot: Rollback progress: 3/5 shards complete
deploybot: Rollback complete. EU canary service-worker at 2025.04.28-stable.
maya: thanks. anita — please prioritize the hotpatch and attach cosign sig to artifact before re-promote.
anita: working on branch hotfix/libcache-pin — building now. CI output: ```BUILD OK
Scanning... vuln-scan: pending```
sasha: I'll run a quick smoke test once build finishes.
legal: keep the release notes neutral; we'll add an internal note referencing "security hardening" only after we confirm fix. No customer-facing blurb until we know impact.
ryan: timeline update: rebuild + sign + scan + smoke ~75m. If green, we can attempt EU re-promote in same window, otherwise schedule for next change window.
maya: thanks all. Create follow-up thread for postmortem. tagging: @sec-bot please create an incident doc ID.
sec-bot: Incident created: INCIDENT-2025-0423-17 — SBOM provenance + high transitive vuln — assigned to security oncall
leo: quick thumbs? :thumbsup: for rollback + timeboxed hotpatch plan
maya: :thumbsup:
ryan: :thumbsup:
anita: :thumbsup:
legal: ack
 (end)
